- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is flat or trending upward, true outcome often reverses within 5–10 days; adjust for 1–3% downward drift if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- When official events are frequent and supply net is negative, model underreacts to sentiment; increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment history by 15–20% for next 7 days.
